The story is tightly woven around central themes of labor, class, value, and identity. Every element—from Nell’s opening line about being underpaid and her twelve years at the Foodfair, to Graham’s patient book restoration and Miss Emily’s fierce, transactional form of love—builds logically toward the climax. When Nell secretly returns to her $11-an-hour cashier job to reclaim a piece of her own identity, she uses the exact confidence and vocabulary Miss Emily instilled in her (including echoing Miss Emily's wedding toast that she "never once took a single thing that wasn't hers") to defend her choice. The beginning, middle, and end seamlessly connect to create a deeply satisfying and unified narrative.
